articles.title: Test machine publishers through their real tools
articles.excerpt: Ahnii! A machine publisher can look least-privileged on paper and still be wrong in both directions. It may carry an administrative permission it never needed, or it may fail in production because a l…
articles.body: Ahnii! A machine publisher can look least-privileged on paper and still be wrong in both directions. It may carry an administrative permission it never needed, or it may fail in production because a lower-level framework check requires a capability nobody included. The useful test is not a list of permission strings. It is the real publishing workflow, executed through the same registered tools and authorization handler the machine will use in production. A recent RHT Circle publishing change provides a compact example. The application has an automated article publisher. It can create drafts, publish and retract articles, and upload images. It must not administer every node or media item, create unrelated content, or let anonymous callers use the same tools.

articles.title: Managed PostgreSQL for Kubernetes apps | Kupe Cloud
articles.excerpt: Your app needs Postgres. The familiar Kubernetes route is to install a database operator, choose its size, arrange TLS, put credentials somewhere the app can reach, and keep the whole arrangement upgr…
articles.body: Your app needs Postgres. The familiar Kubernetes route is to install a database operator, choose its size, arrange TLS, put credentials somewhere the app can reach, and keep the whole arrangement upgraded. That is real work, and we would rather not make every team repeat it on every cluster. It also means the database competes with your app for the cluster's CPU and memory, and you secure it on your own. Kupe now provides managed PostgreSQL databases. You create a database for your account, then bind a role into the namespace where an app runs. The namespace receives a Service and a credentials Secret; the app mounts the Secret and uses the supplied connection URI. We built the feature around that last step. Creating a database is the easy half.

articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight (Oct. 21-22) in the light of a waxing moon. Here's what to expect from one of Autumn's greatest natural light shows.
articles.body: Don't miss the Orionid meteor shower peak tonight (Oct. 21-22) as tiny shards of Halley's Comet collide with Earth's atmosphere to carve fiery streaks through the Autumn sky! But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show? The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061. Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA . However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight.

articles.body: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales. The sticking points Running a nuclear reactor in space may sound like lunacy, but it’s not.
